cards.title: Word Formation, Affixes
rule: Definition: Word Formation and Derivational Morphology (ስነ-ቅርጺ ቃላትን ምምስራት ሓደሽቲ ቃላትን) refers to the processes of creating new words from existing root words by adding prefixes and suffixes, thereby modifying their semantic meaning or converting them into different grammatical word classes.

English word formation is heavily dependent on concatenative morphology, where prefixes (added to the beginning of a root) and suffixes (added to the end of a root) are sequentially attached to a base form ($$\text{Prefix} + \text{Root} + \text{Suffix}$$). In contrast, Tigrinya uses a Semitic root-and-pattern (consonantal root) system. In Tigrinya, word class conversion and nominalization are primarily achieved through internal vowel melody shifts and consonant doubling within a triconsonantal root (e.g., the root {s-b-r} meaning 'to break' produces "ስባር" [broken piece] or "ስባረ" [fracture]) rather than the linear affixation typical of English. This fundamental morphological difference is a major conceptual hurdle for Tigrinya-speaking students, who must transition from an internal consonantal modification system to a linear, suffix-based word-building system.

examples.text: She goes to school every day.
She go to school every day.

cards.title: Notes
body: Definition: Word Formation and Derivational Morphology (ስነ-ቅርጺ ቃላትን ምምስራት ሓደሽቲ ቃላትን) refers to the processes of creating new words from existing root words by adding prefixes and suffixes, thereby modifying their semantic meaning or converting them into different grammatical word classes.

English word formation is heavily dependent on concatenative morphology, where prefixes (added to the beginning of a root) and suffixes (added to the end of a root) are sequentially attached to a base form ($$\text{Prefix} + \text{Root} + \text{Suffix}$$). In contrast, Tigrinya uses a Semitic root-and-pattern (consonantal root) system. In Tigrinya, word class conversion and nominalization are primarily achieved through internal vowel melody shifts and consonant doubling within a triconsonantal root (e.g., the root {s-b-r} meaning 'to break' produces "ስባር" [broken piece] or "ስባረ" [fracture]) rather than the linear affixation typical of English. This fundamental morphological difference is a major conceptual hurdle for Tigrinya-speaking students, who must transition from an internal consonantal modification system to a linear, suffix-based word-building system.

Nominalization (ምስራሕ ስማት) is the process of converting verbs or adjectives into nouns. Verbs are converted to nouns using suffixes like *-ment, -tion, -sion, -ance, -ence, -al* ($$\text{Verb} + \text{Suffix} \rightarrow \text{Noun}$$, e.g., *agree* $$\rightarrow$$ *agreement*, *decide* $$\rightarrow$$ *decision*, *assist* $$\rightarrow$$ *assistance*). Adjectives are converted to nouns using suffixes like *-ness, -ity, -dom, -hood, -ship* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{Suffix} \rightarrow \text{Noun}$$, e.g., *happy* $$\rightarrow$$ *happiness*, *pure* $$\rightarrow$$ *purity*, *free* $$\rightarrow$$ *freedom*). National examinations frequently test these nominalized forms in subject and object slots, requiring students to identify spelling adjustments (e.g., dropping 'y' to 'i' in *happiness* or consonant shifts in *decide* $$\rightarrow$$ *decision*).

cards.title: Build words with affixes
cards.problem: Complete with a form of the word in brackets: "The plan was ____ (success) because the team was ____ (organise) and ____ (honest) was rewarded."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the needed word class.** After "was" and before "because" → adjective; after "was" describing the team → adjective (participle); subject of a verb → noun.
**Step 2: Add the suffix.** success + -ful → successful; organise + -ed → organised; honest + -y → honesty.
**Tip:** -ful/-ous/-ive make adjectives; -ness/-ity/-ment/-y make nouns; un-/dis-/in- change the meaning, not the class.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The sudden ________ of the school principal surprised both the teachers and the students.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The blank follows the article 'The' and the adjective 'sudden', requiring a noun ($$\text{Article} + \text{Adjective} + \text{Noun}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose the verb 'depart' (Option A) due to direct translation. Only the nominalized form 'departure' (Option B), formed by adding the suffix '-ure' to the verb 'depart', is grammatically correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ባዶ ቦታ ድሕሪ 'The' (ኣንቀጽ) ከምኡ ውን ድሕሪ 'sudden' (ቅጽል) ስለ ዝመጸ፡ ብግድን ስም (noun) ክኸውን ኣለዎ። እቲ 'depart' (ምኻድ) ዝብል ግሲ ናብ ስም ክቕየር ከሎ ድማ 'departure' (Option B - ምኻድ/ምስጓም) ይኸውን። 'depart' ምጥቃም ሰዋስዋዊ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The instructions provided by the examiner were highly ________, which caused many candidates to make mistakes.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context 'which caused many candidates to make mistakes' indicates a negative adjective is required to describe the instructions.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often struggle with negative prefixes and choose 'disclear' (Option C) or 'inclear' (Option D). The correct negative prefix for the adjective 'clear' is 'un-', forming 'unclear' (Option B).

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ተመሃሮ ጌጋ ከም ዝገበሩ ስለ ዝገለጸ፡ እቲ መግለጺ 'ዘይነጸረ' (negative adjective) ክኸውን ኣለዎ። ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ን 'clear' (ንጹር) ኣሉታዊ ክንገብሮ ከለና እንጥቅመሉ ቅድመ-መጣበቕታ 'un-' ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'unclear' (Option B - ዘይንጹር) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Choose the correct form: "Her ____ to help others is admirable."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** After "Her" (a possessive) we need a noun.

**Step 2:** willing + -ness → willingness.

**Step 3:** "willing" is an adjective and "willingly" an adverb.

**Tip:** Look at the position: after an article → noun; before a noun → adjective; describing a verb → adverb; after "to" or a subject → verb. Then add the suffix that makes that part of speech.

questions.q: To solve this complex algebraic equation, you must first ________ the brackets.
questions.label: 4. To solve this complex algebraic equation, you must first ___
why: The blank follows the modal verb 'must' and the adverb 'first', requiring a base verb ($$\text{Modal} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.label: 5. His behavior was highly ________; he did not attend any of t

questions.q: The scientific ________ of the laboratory equipment is essential for obtaining accurate research results.
questions.label: 6. The scientific ________ of the laboratory equipment is essen
why: The blank follows the article 'The' and the adjective 'scientific', requiring a noun ($$\text{Article} + \text{Adjective} + \text{Noun}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: It is completely ________ to drive a vehicle on public roads without having a valid driving license.
questions.label: 7. It is completely ________ to drive a vehicle on public roads

questions.q: She completed her chemistry experiment ________, and she was highly praised by the professor.
questions.label: 8. She completed her chemistry experiment ________, and she was

questions.q: The university plans to ________ its library catalogue by introducing a new digital search system.
questions.label: 9. The university plans to ________ its library catalogue by in

questions.q: The sudden ________ of clean drinking water in the region has caused severe health concerns.
questions.label: 10. The sudden ________ of clean drinking water in the region ha
why: The blank follows the article 'The' and the adjective 'sudden', requiring a noun ($$\text{Article} + \text{Adjective} + \text{Noun}$$).

questions.q: The sudden ____ of the principal surprised everyone.
questions.label: 11. The sudden ____ of the principal surprised everyone.
why: After "The sudden" we need a noun (sudden is an adjective).
The other forms are verbs or participles.
questions.tip: Look at the position: after an article → noun; before a noun → adjective; describing a verb → adverb; after "to" or a subject → verb. Then add the suffix that makes that part of speech.

questions.q: The instructions were highly ____ for beginners.
questions.label: 12. The instructions were highly ____ for beginners.
why: After "were highly" we need an adjective.
questions.tip: Look at the position: after an article → noun; before a noun → adjective; describing a verb → adverb; after "to" or a subject → verb. Then add the suffix that makes that part of speech.

questions.q: She spoke ____ about her experiences in the war.
questions.label: 13. She spoke ____ about her experiences in the war.
why: The word describes how she spoke (a verb).
Adverbs often end in -ly: emotional → emotionally.
The others are nouns or an adjective.
questions.tip: Look at the position: after an article → noun; before a noun → adjective; describing a verb → adverb; after "to" or a subject → verb. Then add the suffix that makes that part of speech.

questions.label: 14. Which prefix makes the opposite of "legal"?
why: Before words starting with "l", the negative prefix is usually "il-".

questions.label: 15. Correct the error: "The government wants to modern the farming methods."

similar.q: Find a word with an adjective suffix.

why: "un-" is a negative prefix: unproductive = not productive.
"production" is a noun with the suffix -tion; "hopeful" has the suffix -ful.

questions.q: He was ____ for his kindness.
questions.label: 19. He was ____ for his kindness.
why: The meaning is that people respected him: a passive past participle.
"respectful" = showing respect; "respectable" = decent; "respective" = relating to each.
questions.tip: Look at the position: after an article → noun; before a noun → adjective; describing a verb → adverb; after "to" or a subject → verb. Then add the suffix that makes that part of speech.

questions.q: True or false: The suffix "-less" means "without".
questions.label: 20. True or false: The suffix "-less" means "without".
why: True. "-less" means without: careless = without care; hopeless = without hope.
questions.tip: Look at the position: after an article → noun; before a noun → adjective; describing a verb → adverb; after "to" or a subject → verb. Then add the suffix that makes that part of speech.
